subject: Resilience proofpoints & next experiments for inference stack
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@vendexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Resilience proofpoints & next experiments for inference stack

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next experiments focused on the reliability vectors you flagged. High level: you want a short, evidence-driven comparison between Redwood and the hyperscaler endpoints on realistic traffic so your infra team can sign off on failover and throttling behavior.

Recap (call highlights):
- Primary ask: prove graceful degradation under rate-limited / partial-region failure scenarios.
- Secondary: compare error budgets and effective availability (P99/P95) during steady and burst traffic.
- Constraints: Vendexa must avoid any production data in the test; you can provide sampled traffic or synthetic replay.

What we propose next (paired experiments):
1) Baseline latency & cold-starts: execute a 30-minute steady-state replay at your 95th-percentile traffic level to capture cold-start and P95/P99 latency on both Redwood-hosted and hyperscaler-managed endpoints.
2) Throttle window: apply an intentional rate limit (50% of normal RPS) for 15 minutes on the hyperscaler endpoint and on Redwood (to emulate quota pressure) and measure error-rate curves and queueing/backpressure behavior.
3) Regional failover: bring down the primary region for 10 minutes to validate automatic routing/fallback and KV cache warmup effects.
4) Error-budget burn: run a synthetic error-injection sweep to estimate time-to-recover and error-budget consumption.

Deliverables from Redwood: test matrix (attached), raw token-level traces, region-level availability charts, and a short one-page executive summary with clear pass/fail criteria for your infra team.

Attachments: 20270522-recap-slides.pdf (call slides), resilience-test-matrix.csv (test steps + metrics).

Ask from Vendexa: a sample traffic capture (S3 presigned link or small dataset), a test API key with limited scope, and a point of contact on the infra side to greenlight regional failover tests.

Proposed windows: May 25–27 (PDT) — Ben and Marissa from our side are available for setup and live monitoring. If that doesn't work, tell me a preferred 2-hour window and we'll adapt.

I pasted a slightly more technical test plan in the attached CSV; Ben will follow up on timings and the data collection hooks.

Short next steps:
- You: share traffic sample + infra POC for failover 
- Us: schedule run, share exact test script and monitoring dashboards

Thanks — looking forward to proving the resilience story.

—
Sofia Ivanova

Thanks Sofia — this is helpful and aligns with what we need. A few clarifying Qs before we lock windows:

1) Rate limits: can you confirm Redwood's throttling behavior when a tenant exceeds a burst window? Specifically, do you return 429s immediately, queue behind a leaky-bucket, or apply backpressure via connection resets? We need to document expected client-side behavior.
2) KV cache behavior during failover: does Redwood reconstruct caches in the fallback region from remote checkpoints or is there a cold-warm start penalty we should budget for?
3) Data handling: we will provide anonymized request payloads only; confirm Redwood will not persist any of the payload beyond the scoped test and that logs will be redacted.

I'll upload a 5k-request sample to S3 and share the presigned link shortly (avoid PII). We can likely do May 26 for the first run (window: 09:00–11:00 PDT).

If you can provide a short paragraph we can copy into our security team describing the failover test (so they approve the window), that would speed things up.

—Olivia
Olivia Park, Senior Engineering Manager
Vendexa
olivia.park@vendexa.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@vendexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Resilience proofpoints & next experiments for inference stack

Olivia — great questions, answers below (short form) and we'll follow up with the technical paragraph for your security approvers.

1) Throttling behavior: Redwood uses a hybrid approach depending on route config. Default behavior for tenant-level spikes is graceful rate limiting that returns 429 when token budget is exceeded; we also support configurable queuing windows for short bursts (up to 10s) and adaptive backpressure that reduces batch sizes to maintain latency SLOs. For the test matrix we'll run both modes so you can see the differences.

2) KV cache in failover: caches are maintained per-region; during a regional failover Redwood will route requests to the fallback region and we warm the KV cache using recent prefixes (if allowed by your policy). There is a measurable cold-warm penalty on first N requests in the fallback region (~1–3 extra tokens of compute for heavy context cases) — we'll capture that in the run and annotate it in the summary.

3) Data handling: confirmed — test payloads will be ephemeral. We will redact any PII at ingest, logs from the test runs can be scoped to request IDs only, and we will not retain raw payloads beyond 72 hours unless you request otherwise. We can put this in writing in the PoC addendum.

Attached: resilience-test-matrix.csv (detailed steps + metrics + pass/fail thresholds). Ben — can you confirm the exact monitoring hooks we need to ship and whether we require an agent on Vendexa infra for region-level failover? Marissa — I'll need you to own the failover playbook and annotations in the final report.

Proposed test script highlights (short):
- Warm-up: 10 minutes at 25% RPS
- Baseline run: 30 minutes at target RPS
- Throttle window: 15 minutes at 50% RPS (with 429s enabled)
- Failover: switch traffic to fallback region for 10 minutes
- Recovery: monitor 30 minutes post-failover for cache rebuild curves

If all good, let's lock May 26 09:00–11:00 PDT. I'll circulate a short note for your security approvers.

—Sofia
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Olivia — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few implementation details from the engineering side:

- Monitoring hooks: please expose a short-lived ingestion endpoint or provide an S3 feed (presigned link is fine). We need request timestamps, prompt length, and an opaque request ID. We'll attach our trace id to responses so you can reconcile.
- Cold-start metrics: we'll capture cold-start rates as the percent of requests with first-token latency > 2x baseline and report P50/P95/P99 for both token and response times.
- 429 behavior: Redwood will return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header when limits are exceeded. For the test we'll run two sub-cases: strict-429 mode and queued-mode (10s leaky-queue). We'll graph error-rate vs latency to show the tradeoffs.
- Failover checklist: to simulate region outage we will coordinate with your infra POC to withdraw routing from the primary region and trigger our automatic fallback. No production config changes required on your side — you only need to validate the route cut in the test window.

I'll be on the call May 26 and will run the test harness. Marissa, can you prepare the resilience report template (one page exec + 3 appendix charts)?

Ben
